newsitem.title: ITALY: Centre-right leads in Milan and Turin-tv polls.
newsitem.headline: Centre-right leads in Milan and Turin-tv polls.

text.p: Candidates backed by Italy's main centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance led in mayoral races in the big northern cities of Milan and Turin after the first round of local elections on Sunday, television exit polls showed.

In Milan, Italy's financial capital and the key contest in voting in more than 1,100 towns and cities, outgoing mayor Marco Formentini of the separatist Northern League finished third and was knocked out of the second round run-off, the polls said.

The exit polls, by the Abacus Institute for broadcasters RAI and Fininvest, gave Formentini 17 to 21 percent of the vote to 38 to 42 percent for centre-right candidate Gabriele Albertini and 23 to 30 for Aldo Fumagalli of Italy's governing centre-left Olive Tree coalition. The two face a run-off on May 11.

In Turin, outgoing mayor Valentino Castellani of the Olive Tree bloc was narrowly beaten into second place by Freedom Alliance challenger Raffaele Costa, according to the exit polls. Both enter the second round.
Sunday's municipal voting, involving about one-fifth of the national electorate, were the biggest test of support since a centre-left general election win last April.

The exit polls showed the centre-left ahead in mayoral races in the cities of Trieste and Ancona, with the centre-right in the lead in Catanzaro and a neck-and-neck race in the city of Reggio Calabria.
